EBP.name: Evading the Burden of Proof
EBP.explanation: This fallacy occurs when someone makes a claim but refuses to provide evidence to support it, shifting the burden of proof to others

ST.name: Strawman
ST.explanation: This involves misrepresenting someone's argument to make it easier to attack or refute than the original argument

FAUT.name: Improper Criteria
FAUT.explanation: This fallacy is citing an authority on a topic who is not actually an expert in that field

RH.name: Red Herring
RH.explanation: This fallacy involves diverting attention from the real issue by introducing an irrelevant topic

CP.name: Cherry Picking
CP.explanation: Selectively presenting evidence that supports one's argument while ignoring evidence that contradicts it

FA.name: False Analogy
FA.explanation: Making a misleading comparison between two things that are not truly comparable

HG.name: Hasty Generalization
HG.explanation: Making a generalized statement based on a small or unrepresentative sample

PH.name: Post Hoc
PH.explanation: Assuming that because one event followed another, the first event caused the second

FC.name: False Cause
FC.explanation: Mistaking correlation for causation, assuming that because two events occur together, one causes the other

VAG.name: Vagueness
VAG.explanation: Using imprecise, unclear, or ambiguous language in an argument

SAT.name: Setting an Arbitrary Threshold
SAT.explanation: This fallacy occurs when an arbitrary standard is set to judge a phenomenon, without considering the broader context or implications

IDV.name: Issues with Data Validity
IDV.explanation: This fallacy arises when there are concerns about the accuracy and consistency of data, which are either exaggerated or ignored to support a preconceived notion

FASN.name: Failure to Account for Statistical Nuance
FASN.group: Failure to Account for Statistical Nuance
FASN.explanation: This occurs when crucial statistical details are overlooked or simplified in an argument, leading to misleading conclusions

MOSS.name: Misrepresentation of Scientific Studies
MOSS.explanation: This involves exaggerating the significance of certain scientific findings that align with one's beliefs or outright rejecting scientific authority in favor of personal anecdotes or pseudo-science

CI.name: Causal Inference
CI.explanation: Incorrectly attributing cause and effect based on limited or anecdotal evidence

IRC.name: Incorrect Reading of Chart
IRC.explanation: Misinterpreting visual data due to visual distortions or incorrect assumptions
